question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping maintains firm control over the Chinese Communist Party and key institutions through extensive purges, loyal appointments to the Politburo and military, and the absence of any designated successor or visible factional challenges. Analysts note he is positioned to secure a fourth term at the 2027 Party Congress, with leadership discussions focused on post-Xi transitions rather than near-term removal. Recent developments, including ongoing anti-corruption actions and stability in elite politics despite economic pressures, reinforce trader consensus that abrupt ouster before 2027 remains improbable. Even so, low-probability shifts could arise from sudden health events, severe economic or social crises eroding elite support, or unexpected internal security disruptions.

Ossoff’s market gains despite public denials of interest illustrate how speculation and perceived electability in swing-state contexts can shift implied probabilities quickly.
